diagnostic_evidence.quote: U_\theta(x,t) = (1 - \tau(t)) U_0(x) + \tau(t) \mathcal{N}_\theta(x,t),
This construction guarantees $U_\theta(x,0) \equiv U_0(x)$, eliminating the initial condition error term from the convergence analysis.
for which the entropy solution consists of a single shock propagating with Rankine--Hugoniot speed $s=\frac{1}{2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For every discontinuous initial datum used in the paper's shock tests, the ansatz bakes a jump of height $(1-\tau(t))J$ at the initial discontinuity location into $U_\theta(\cdot,t)$ for all $t<T$; the jump cannot move, so the ansatz cannot represent a shock with nonzero Rankine--Hugoniot speed (e.g., the Riemann shock with $s=1/2$). A stationary jump carries a nonzero flux imbalance, so $L_{\mathrm{cons}}$ stays bounded away from zero on control volumes containing the initial discontinuity: hypothesis 3 of thm:added-2 is unsatisfiable in the very regime the method targets, and the reported accurate moving-shock results are inconsistent with the construction. The baked-in jump also makes $U_\theta$ non-smooth, breaking the integration-by-parts/divergence-theorem manipulations behind the residuals and Lemma lem:added-1, and making $L_{\mathrm{TVD}}=\sup_t\int|\nabla_x U_\theta|dx$ undefined at the jump.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the exact-initial-condition ansatz, parameterize $U_\theta$ directly, add an initial-condition loss term, and keep the $\|U_\theta(\cdot,0)-u_0\|_{L^1}$ term in the Bouchut-Perthame bound (which the theorem statement already displays); the convergence conclusion survives with this additional term.
issues.overall_effect: The method cannot represent moving discontinuities; the convergence theorem's loss-vanishing hypothesis cannot hold for the paper's own Riemann tests; the regularity behind the weak residuals, the TVD term, and Lemma 1 fails for the ansatz output; the reported shock results contradict the construction.
issues.title: Temporal ansatz freezes the initial discontinuity in place and breaks the regularity the analysis needs
issues.why_classification: The repair is local (remove the ansatz, add a standard IC penalty) and the theorem architecture survives with one extra term, but the advertised exact-IC construction and all reported shock results must be revised.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Crucially, boundary conditions are seamlessly integrated into this formulation.
U_\theta\, n_t + F(U_\theta)\cdot n_x

issues.failure_explanation: The residual $R_\theta(D_k)$ is built exclusively from $U_\theta$ and $F(U_\theta)$ evaluated on the network; no prescribed boundary data appears anywhere in the loss functional. Evaluating the network's own flux on a boundary face measures the network's internal balance, not any mismatch with imposed boundary data, so boundary conditions are not enforced at all. The sentence advertises a capability the construction does not have.

failure_location.quote: When a boundary face of a control volume $D_k$ coincides with the physical boundary of the domain $\Omega_x$, the flux integration across this face directly enforces the prescribed boundary conditions naturally through the evaluation of $R_\theta(D_k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either correct the prose to state that boundary conditions are not imposed, or modify the loss so boundary faces use prescribed fluxes (e.g., substitute the prescribed boundary flux for $F(U_\theta)$ on physical-boundary faces, or add a boundary-mismatch penalty); the latter requires revalidation.
issues.overall_effect: As described, the method solves only the Cauchy problem; boundary traces are unconstrained for initial-boundary value problems, and the numerical section never states which boundary conditions were used. The convergence theorem is unaffected (Bouchut-Perthame needs no boundary conditions), but an advertised feature is illusory.
issues.title: Claim that boundary conditions are enforced is false: no prescribed boundary data enters the loss
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence correction removes the false claim but withdraws an advertised feature; genuinely enforcing boundary conditions requires new loss terms and revalidation, which is more than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To guarantee this condition, we introduce a TVD regularization term:
L_{\mathrm{TVD}}(\theta) \approx \max_{j=1,\dots,N_t} \sum_{k=1}^{N_x-1} |U_\theta(x_{k+1}, t_j) - U_\theta(x_k, t_j)|,
The TVD regularization guarantees $\sup_{t \in [0,T]} TV(U_\theta(\cdot, t)) \leq M$ for some constant $M$;

issues.failure_explanation: Two defects. (i) Minimizing $\sup_t\int_\Omega|\nabla_x U_\theta|dx$ does not enforce any uniform upper bound on the total variation: with weight $\lambda_{\mathrm{TVD}}=1$ competing against the conservation and entropy losses, the term penalizes variation and biases the network toward constants, the opposite of the shock-resolving regime targeted, and it cannot deliver the bound assumed in item 2 of thm:added-2. (ii) The stochastic estimator replaces the spatial integral by differences at random unordered points, which is not a consistent approximation of TV: for a layer of width $\delta$ and jump $J$, $TV=J$ but the expected random-pair difference is $O(J\delta)$, so sharp features are underestimated exactly in the regime where the BV bound matters; the formula is also one-dimensional only. For the ansatz with discontinuous $U_0$, $|\nabla_x U_\theta|$ does not even exist at the baked-in jump, so the term is ill-defined and only the invalid estimator remains.

failure_location.quote: \State Sample a random cloud of points and compute $L_{\mathrm{TVD}}$ as in Section~\ref{sec:tvd}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the penalty by a soft constraint such as $\lambda\max(0,\widehat{TV}(U_\theta)-M)^2$ (or a barrier/projection) with a consistent TV estimator (ordered quadrature grid or fixed mesh), and re-tune the weights; the theorem remains conditional on the resulting bound.
issues.overall_effect: The training objective contains a term that biases against shocks and cannot produce the uniform BV bound on which the convergence analysis relies; the TV reported during training is not a total variation. The convergence theorem survives only as a conditional whose hypothesis the algorithm does not deliver.
issues.title: TVD regularization penalizes variation instead of bounding it, and the stochastic estimator does not estimate total variation
issues.why_classification: Requires a new regularizer, a consistent estimator, and re-tuning — a contained but nontrivial change; the advertised guarantee is withdrawn, though the conditional theorem survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's central step is false. For smooth $U_\theta$, integration by parts gives $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}(U_\theta) = -\int\int \varphi\,\operatorname{sgn}(U_\theta-k)\,r_\theta$ with the strong residual $r_\theta = \partial_t U_\theta + \nabla_x\cdot F(U_\theta)$: a bulk quantity weighted by the arbitrary test function. The boundary sum of the truncation flux $(|U_\theta-k|\varphi,\, q_k(U_\theta)\varphi)$ vanishes identically (internal faces cancel, $\varphi$ has compact support), and in any case the truncation flux uses the Kruzhkov fluxes $|U_\theta-k|$ and $\operatorname{sgn}(U_\theta-k)(F(U_\theta)-F(k))$ for a free parameter $k$, whereas the losses use the physical fluxes $U_\theta,F(U_\theta)$ and the physical entropy pair $\eta(U_\theta),q(U_\theta)$, which do not involve $k$. Counterexample: on the trivial partition $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$ take (within the method's own ansatz, $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi N x)$, $\mathcal{N}_\theta\equiv0$) $U_\theta(x,t)=(1-\tau(t))\sin(2\pi N x)$ for Burgers. Then $R_\theta(D)=0$ and $E_\theta(D)=-(1-\tau(0))^2/4<0$, so $L_{\mathrm{cons}}=L_{\mathrm{ent}}=0$, but with $k=0$ and $\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{2\pi N}(1-\cos(2\pi N x))$ (tapered; admissible) $\mathcal{R}_{k,\varphi}=\frac{1}{12}-o(1)>0$, so $E_R(U_\theta)>0$ while the claimed bound's right side is $0$. The proof also drops a factor $\sqrt{N_D}$ in the discrete Cauchy--Schwarz step (since $L_{\mathrm{cons}}=\frac{1}{N_D}\sum_i|R_i|^2/|D_i|$ gives $\sum_i|R_i|\le\sqrt{N_D\,|\Omega\times(0,T)|\,L_{\mathrm{cons}}}}$), and its partition hypothesis does not cover the algorithm's overlapping multi-scale sampling, for which $\sum_i|D_i|\neq|\Omega\times(0,T)|$.

failure_location.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals, corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; a correct bound of the dual-norm Kruzhkov truncation error by control-volume boundary losses would require a genuinely new argument (e.g., controlling the strong residual $r_\theta$ in negative norms from the losses, plus a Kruzhkov-entropy loss for all $k$), and the advertised explicit rate is lost.
issues.overall_effect: The main convergence theorem's Step 3, the advertised explicit $L^1$ rate $1/4$, the abstract/introduction claim of the first explicit $L^1$ convergence rate for a mesh-free control-volume PINN, and the unlabelled optimality remark all rest on this lemma and are unsupported.
issues.title: Lemma 1's bound of the continuous truncation error by the network losses is false
issues.why_classification: The paper's central theoretical contribution is false as stated with an explicit counterexample; every resolution needs essentially new proof architecture and the explicit-rate guarantee is abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \leq C \sqrt{TV(u_0) M} \cdot \left[ |\Omega \times (0,T)|^{1/2} \left( \sqrt{L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)} + \sqrt{L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)} \right) \right]^{1/2}.

issues.failure_explanation: The Bouchut-Perthame estimate is linear in $\sqrt{E_R(v)}$ (calibration: vanishing-viscosity solutions have $E_R\sim\varepsilon$ and optimal $L^1$ error $\sim\sqrt{\varepsilon}$), i.e., of the form $C\sqrt{TV(u_0)\sup_t TV(v)\,E_R(v)}$; the displayed formula weakens the dependence to $E_R(v)^{1/4}$. The statement is therefore not the cited theorem, and it does not support the application in thm:added-2 Step 4, which algebraically uses the correct form: the displayed substitution replaces $\sqrt{\sqrt{E_R}}$ by $[\sqrt{|\Omega_T|}(\sqrt{L_{\mathrm{cons}}}+\sqrt{L_{\mathrm{ent}}})]^{1/2}$, i.e., it uses $\sqrt{TV\,M\,E_R}$, not the stated $\sqrt{TV\,M\sqrt{E_R}}$. With the estimate as stated, Step 4 would only yield the weaker rate $L_{\mathrm{cons}}^{1/8}+L_{\mathrm{ent}}^{1/8}$.

issues.overall_effect: Internal inconsistency between the stated Bouchut-Perthame estimate and its use; the claimed $1/4$ rate follows only from the correct estimate, not from the one displayed.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem invokes the Bouchut-Perthame estimate, which is proved for scalar conservation laws and requires the approximate solution to be bounded. The statement neither restricts \eqref{eq:conservation_law} to $m=1$ — it is stated for the $\mathbb{R}^m$ system, for which 'the entropy solution' is not even well-defined in general — nor assumes any $L^\infty$ bound on $U_\theta = (1-\tau)U_0 + \tau\mathcal{N}_\theta$ (a bound on $U_0$ alone does not bound the network part). The scalar-only caveat appears only in the prose before the section. The proof therefore applies the invoked estimate outside its hypotheses.

issues.failure_explanation: The error columns are labelled by time ($t=0.0, 0.5, 1.0$) and captioned 'Relative errors at different times', but every method's $t=0.0$ errors are nonzero (e.g., $E_{L^1}=8.07\mathrm{e}{-3}$, $E_{L^\infty}=7.95\mathrm{e}{-1}$ for WE-PINNs on the Riemann problem). Under the temporal ansatz, $U_\theta(\cdot,0)=U_0$ exactly, so any fixed-time error at $t=0$ vanishes identically. If instead the entries are space-time errors over $\Omega\times(0,t]$, the printed definition (a fixed domain $\Omega_T=\Omega\times(0,T)$) and the column headers are wrong, and the $t=0$ column is degenerate. Either way the reported numbers are inconsistent with the paper's own construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the error definition and column headers to match what was computed (fixed-time errors, which must read zero at $t=0$ under the ansatz) or correct the data; if the experiments did not use the ansatz, the method section must be revised accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical evidence for the flagship Riemann test is internally inconsistent with the method as defined; reproducibility of the reported accuracy is undermined.
issues.title: Reported t=0 errors contradict the exact initial-condition ansatz

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
abla_U q^{(j)}(U) = 
abla_U \eta(U)\,
abla_U F^{(j)}(U), \qquad j=1,\dots,d.
In all cases, the entropy functions are convex and the corresponding entropy fluxes satisfy the compatibility condition with the physical flux, ensuring consistency with the entropy inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: For the shallow-water flux $F(h,hu)=(hu,\,hu^2+\tfrac12gh^2)$, the convex function $\eta=\tfrac12hu^2+\tfrac12gh^2$ has entropy flux $q=\tfrac12hu^3+gh^2u$ (equivalently $q=u(\tfrac12hu^2+gh^2)$; in 2D, $q^{(j)}=u^{(j)}(\tfrac12h|\mathbf u|^2+gh^2)$), not $q=\eta\,u=\tfrac12hu^3+\tfrac12gh^2u$. The pair printed in Appendix C fails the compatibility relation, so even for smooth exact solutions $\partial_t\eta(U)+\partial_x q(U)=-ghu\,h_x-\tfrac12gh^2u_x\neq0$: the entropy loss used in the dam-break and 2D shallow-water experiments is not an entropy inequality and penalizes exact solutions, and the closing claim that all listed pairs are compatible is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $q(U)=\eta(U)\mathbf{u}$ by $q^{(j)}(U)=u^{(j)}\big(\tfrac12 h|\mathbf u|^2+g h^2\big)$ (in 1D, $q=\tfrac12hu^3+gh^2u$); a direct one-line correction.
issues.overall_effect: Entropy-admissibility enforcement for the shallow-water experiments is mathematically vacuous, and the claim that all listed entropy pairs are compatible is false; the scalar convergence theory is unaffected.
issues.title: Shallow-water entropy flux in Appendix C fails the compatibility condition
issues.why_classification: A one-line formula correction restores a valid entropy pair; no theorem, rate, or algorithm contract depends on the wrong formula.
